chunks: Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from Al-Hasan ibn Ali ibn Fazzal, from Ali ibn Uqba, from his father, from Muyassar ibn Abdul Aziz, from Abu Ja'far (peace be upon him) who said:
He said: 'O Muyassar! Marry at night, for Allah has made it for rest, and do not seek a need at night, for the night is dark.'
Then he said: 'Surely, for the night visitor there is a great right, and for the owner there is a great right.'
ai.seo_question: What is the recommended etiquette for marriage and visiting at night according to Shia hadith?
ai.summary: In this hadith from al-Kafi, Imam al-Sadiq (peace be upon him) highlights the night as a time of tranquility (sakana) suitable for marital intimacy, while cautioning against undertaking urgent matters due to the cover of darkness. This teaching underscores the spiritual and physical sanctity of the marital bond, linking it to the Quranic concept of spouses as garments of comfort and protection. The mention of 'rights' emphasizes the mutual obligations inherent in the marital contract, reinforcing the social and ethical dimensions of marriage in Shia jurisprudence.

en.hubeali:
Muhammad Bin Yahya, from Ahmad Bin Muhammad, from Al Hassan Bin Ali Bin Fazzal, from Ali Bin Uqba, from his father, from Muyassar Bin Abdul Aziz,
(It has been narrated) from Abu Ja’far<sup>asws</sup> having said:
‘O Muyassar! Get married at night, for Allah<sup>azwj</sup> Made it for rest, but do not seek a need at night, for the night is dark’.
Then he<sup>asws</sup> said: ‘Surely, for the night visitor there is a great right, and for the owner there is a great right’.
en.sarwar: 3. Muhammad ibn Yahya has narrated from Ahmad ibn Muhammad from al-Hassan ibn Ali from ibn Faddal from Ali ibn ‘Uqbah from his father from Muyassir ibn ‘Abd al-’Aziz who has said the following: “Abu Ja‘far, ‘Alayhi al-Salam, once said to me, ‘O Muyassir, marry during the night because Allah has made the night for comfort and do not seek for any of your needs during the night; the night is dark.
He (the narrator) has said, that he (the Imam) then said, ‘One who comes during the night has a great right and the companion has a great right.’”
